questions.question: What is a Spring Boot starter?
options: A class you extend to start the application
A small dependency that pulls in a tested group of libraries for one task
A plugin that generates Java code
A command that starts the embedded server
questions.explanation: A starter has almost no code; it brings a matched set of libraries, such as everything needed for a web app.

questions.question: In Spring Boot 4.1, which starter should a new REST API project use for Spring MVC with Tomcat?
options: spring-boot-starter-web
spring-web
spring-boot-starter-tomcat
spring-boot-starter-webmvc
questions.explanation: spring-boot-starter-webmvc is the Boot 4 web starter; spring-boot-starter-web is deprecated in its favour.

questions.question: A project has only spring-boot-starter-webmvc and spring-boot-starter-actuator, and no health code. What does GET /actuator/health return?
options: A reply containing "status":"UP"
404 Not Found, because no controller maps that path
An empty page
500, because health checks need a database
questions.explanation: The Actuator starter switches on the health endpoint by itself through auto-configuration.

questions.question: A developer excludes spring-boot-starter-tomcat from the web starter to use Jetty, but forgets to add spring-boot-starter-jetty. What happens when the app runs?
options: Jetty starts anyway, because it is the default
The build fails with a missing dependency error
The app logs Started ... and then exits, because there is no web server to keep it running
Tomcat starts, because exclusions are ignored at runtime
questions.explanation: With no server library left, Spring Boot starts a non-web application that finishes and exits straight away.

questions.question: Which artifact name follows the convention for a third-party (community) starter?
options: spring-boot-starter-mybatis
mybatis-spring-boot-starter
spring-mybatis-starter
starter-mybatis-spring
questions.explanation: Official starters are spring-boot-starter-*; third-party starters put their own name first.
